question: Should independent module results be internal objects linked into one artifact or independently validated cdbc products?
decision: Emit one cdbc 0.1 module artifact per graph module with canonical-path identity, dependency metadata, and source-order insertion markers; retain the existing linked-program artifact as the default output.

artifact_contract.entry_order: Present only for entry modules and ordered by graph entry discovery.
artifact_contract.dependency_marker: target identity, import or re_export kind, requested path, and local main instruction offset
artifact_contract.core_sections: The module's own constants, names, main, functions, and optional debug sections use the linked cdbc 0.1 grammar.

link_contract.dependency_walk: Expand dependency markers in source order and load each identity at most once.
link_contract.rebasing: A linker must rebase local registers, constants, names, functions, jumps, and debug references while preserving marker insertion offsets.
link_contract.current_status: Rust link loads the product directory, selects contiguous entry_order values, expands source-ordered dependency markers once, rebases local bytecode and debug references, and writes a linked cdbc 0.1 program; cache reuse is later M3B work.

compatibility_boundary.linked_artifact: Existing cdbc 0.1 output is byte-for-byte unchanged and remains executable.
compatibility_boundary.module_artifact: Rust dump parses and canonicalizes it; Rust run rejects it before VM execution until linked.
compatibility_boundary.identity: Canonical paths are serialized as product identities; snapshot-local numeric module IDs are filename/session transport names only.
compatibility_boundary.interfaces: Module interfaces remain in-memory TypeChecker records in this slice.
compatibility_boundary.cache: No persistent cache key or invalidation policy is introduced.

out_of_scope: replacement of the default linked-program emitter
